title: Non-penetrating World Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.27963v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. translated_abstract: 我们研究了交互式视频世界模型中防止物体穿透这一新问题。为了解现有模型如何应对该问题，我们提出了NoPeBench，一个评估世界模型对物理障碍物响应能力的基准测试。评估结果显示，目前没有任何开源模型能够可靠地防止此类穿透失败。然而令人惊讶的是，这些模型内部已经编码了预测此类违规行为所需的信息。我们发现，扩散Transformer（DiT）的隐藏状态可以预测某个候选动作是否会穿透障碍物。基于这一发现，我们提出了NoPeWorld，一个检测并防止穿透的轻量级框架。具体而言，我们在冻结的DiT隐藏状态之上训练一个小型预测头，用于判断候选动作是否安全，随后将不安全的动作替换为最能保留原始意图的安全动作。尽管方法简洁，NoPeWorld显著减少了……
tldr: 该论文提出NoPeBench基准和NoPeWorld框架，通过在冻结的扩散Transformer隐藏状态上训练小型预测头来检测并替换不安全动作，有效防止交互式视频世界模型中的物体穿透问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces NoPeBench and NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that trains a small prediction head on frozen DiT hidden states to detect and replace unsafe actions, effectively preventing object penetration in interactive video world models.
